reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether cetuximab engaged EGFR. The trial assumed target engagement based on known binding affinity but did not measure it directly. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm downstream EGFR signaling inhibition. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (DFS at 3 years) was not met. Cetuximab arm showed worse DFS than control in both KRAS wild-type (71.5% vs 74.6%) and KRAS mutant (65.0% vs 67.1%) subgroups. OS also trended worse with cetuximab. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Both KRAS wild-type and mutant subgroups showed similar negative trends, suggesting the failure was not population-specific but rather mechanism-related. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Grade 3+ toxicity was significantly higher with cetuximab (73.3% vs 51.1%, p<0.001), but this appears to be tolerability rather than dose-limiting toxicity preventing adequate dosing. The trial was adequately powered with 3397 patients and 3-year follow-up was appropriate for adjuvant setting.

failure_modes.evidence: While target engagement cannot be confirmed without biomarker data, cetuximab is a well-established EGFR antagonist. The failure likely occurred at the clinical translation step - EGFR inhibition may have occurred but did not translate to improved DFS in the adjuvant colon cancer setting, possibly due to redundant survival pathways or inappropriate timing of intervention.

Antibody-dependent cytotoxicity mechanism did not effectively modulate EGFR signaling to produce clinical benefit
